label: original-phase inputs 0/o/j/f/h/3/r (not at t=0)
explanation: Low end of candidate unit 95. It fires almost entirely in the original (input) phase, which holds 94% of activation mass, and peaks at t=1-4. It is mostly driven by the current input token: 0 has a 33% firing rate, then o, j, f, h, 3 and r, each at about 10-19%. It is weak at t=0 and nearly silent at the delimiter and in the copy phase, apart from a small effect when s is being output. Magnitude goes up when the token is the first occurrence in the sequence and when the sequence starts with one of q/s/t/u/v/w. The top examples are 0 or o following an opening run of s/t/v/q/w letters. Still, the same token fires or stays silent depending on earlier context, which suggests hidden-state dependence the predicate cannot capture. Adding first-token, position or first-occurrence conditions raised dev F1 only from 0.42 to 0.43. Dev: precision 0.31, recall 0.62, mass recall 0.75.
